title: 💬 Meta Quietly Launches "Form": A Reddit Clone With Facebook Login and an AI Assistant!
body: 💬 Meta Quietly Launches "Form": A Reddit Clone With Facebook Login and an AI Assistant!
Meta quietly listed a new app called "Form" on Apple's App Store, with no big announcement, no press conference, and no promotional campaign — the app simply appeared in the store out of nowhere.

The app is a discussion platform in the style of Reddit: communities, discussion topics, and moderators — but entry is through a Facebook account, which ties the app from day one to the user's real identity and Meta's advertising machine.

The standout feature is an AI assistant for moderators, helping sort reports, detect spam, and draft replies — the hardest job in community apps, since Reddit's volunteer moderators have struggled for years with spam and organized attacks using limited tools.

Meta is also testing a standalone messaging app called "Direct" in selected markets, after years of building messaging into Instagram. The company's record of copying ideas is mixed: Threads succeeded when it borrowed Instagram's audience at a moment when Twitter was faltering, but it has launched and shut down many apps that never found an audience.

The decisive question is simple: why would a Reddit user move? Reddit's value lies in its communities, its history, and its culture — things you can't copy just by launching an app — and frank discussion depends on the freedom to make a mistake without your words following you to work, while Meta's entire business depends on knowing exactly who you are.
Simply put: Meta wants Reddit's communities without giving up your real identity… and the tension between those two ideas is the heart of the whole story.
Would you join a discussion community that requires a Facebook account?
